newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares dipped on Tuesday, but ignored potentially bearish U.S. housing starts figures, and picked up towards the end with light short-covering, dealers said.

The AEX index of blue chip stocks ended down 3.18 points at 612.94, higher than its opening and than its mid-afternoon low of 608.24, a drop spurred by a rise in U.S. housing starts in November of 9.2 percent. Traders said they had expected the indicator to be barely unchanged.
However, a number or traders were also prepared to dismiss U.S. homestarts as relatively insignificant.
"Housing starts are not that big a figure," one trader said.

However, traders did admit to nerves on the day that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting began. The Federal Reserve's policy-making committee is due to announce its rate decision at about 1915 GMT.
"There's a lot of nervousness about what Greenspan's going to say. Hopefully, he will choose his words carefully," one trader said.
The last public comments from the head of the Federal Reserve, that stock markets must be wary of "irrational exuberance" led to a worldwide stock market crash.
The nervousness led to low Amsterdam stock market volumes and, after late short-covering, a reasonably even fall in individual shares.
The exception was the technological sector to which Monday's Wall Street sell-off filtered through.
The most heavily traded technological stock, in the software firm Baan Company, was down 3.50 guilders to 56.50.
ASM Lithography which makes machines for semi-conductors fell 3.10 guilders to 82.20.
Personal computer maker Tulip dropped 1.50 guilders to 15.60.
"Of the ten biggest losers, about five or six were technology stocks," one trader said.
